float-button.summary: A 44dp circle that floats on the page with the canvas shadow. Flat drops the fill and the shadow for a small action inside a row.
usage: Hold one icon, and give it a label for accessibility: FloatIcon does both for a Lu glyph.
Every floating element carries the canvas shadow, so use this rather than a bare Box with a shadow.
Flat is for small actions inside a row (copy, edit, delete). A sheet's close and back buttons are not flat: they look as they do on the page (rule 70).

capsule-tabs.summary: A white pill of equal segments with a sliding paper pill under the selected one.
usage: Equal segments, one line of text each.
The selected segment slides with the slide curve.
Flat drops the shadow when the pill sits inside a card or a row. In a sheet it keeps its shadow, as on the page (rule 70).

soft-chip.summary: A 36dp outlined pill that fills when selected. An optional count sits in the muted ink.
usage: Use it for filters and choices that can be on or off.
The count is tabular so digits do not move the chip.

underline-tabs.summary: Text tabs on a hairline, the selected one underlined in the accent.
usage: Summary and Description are underline tabs, never a boxed control.
The hairline is under the tabs only, none above.
Each tab is 42dp tall so it is easy to hit.

check.summary: A 22dp rounded box, white with a grey edge, filled with the accent and a white tick once on.
usage: A bare checkbox and a word. No pill, no count.
Pass onClick for a tappable one, null for one that only shows state.

switch.summary: A 52 by 32dp switch: grey track off, accent track on, white thumb with a small shadow.
usage: Give it a label: it is the accessible name.
Disabled dims it to half.

cta-button.summary: The 52dp dark pill that carries one screen's main action.
usage: One per screen, and never an irreversible action: those go behind the more menu.
The label is one line.
Leading and trailing take a Lu icon only when it carries a fact.

pill-button.summary: The quiet 44dp pill for the actions beside a screen's main one: Retry, Stop, Rewrite.
usage: Never the screen's one main action: that is the dark button.
The label is one line; a leading Lu icon only when it carries a fact.
Put it where the thing it acts on is, not in a row of its own.

pill-input.summary: The 52dp raised pill that holds a one-line question or comment, with its send button inside.
usage: Float it over the page at the bottom with 24dp below it, above a fade.
The send button inside is the primary circle; nothing else sits in the pill.
The placeholder says what to type, in a few words.

sheet-field.summary: A text field that lives inside a sheet's white card: the label small and muted over the value, a hairline above.
usage: Put it in a SheetCard, never on the bare sheet or the page.
First drops the hairline above it; a trailing word such as Show is text, never an icon.
Two or more lines makes it a note area for a description or a comment.

sheet.summary: A paper bottom sheet with 24dp top corners, a grabber, and a header of close button and centred title.
usage: Sheets over pages: grouped actions, chat, composer and files open in one.
Content scrolls and a long one pulls all the way up (full).
It is a window, so this page draws its surface inline and opens the real one from a button.

sheet-card.summary: A white 16dp card on a sheet's paper, with a soft shadow.
usage: Put SheetRow children in it.
It is for sheets and grouped screens, one dialect everywhere.

sheet-row.summary: A 52dp row: a 22dp icon column, the label, a trailing value, and a hairline that starts after the icon.
usage: First drops the hairline above it.
Danger colours the label for the action that cannot be undone, which still never sits first.
Iconless spans the hairline across the row and starts the label at the edge.

quick-action.summary: A 72dp tile with an icon over a label, used in rows of equal tiles on a sheet.
usage: Put them in a Row with weight 1 each.
Keep the label to one word.

toast.summary: A dark pill above the bottom bars. It leaves after 2.4 seconds, or 4.2 when it offers an action.
usage: There is one host for the whole app. Show a message with LocalToaster.current.show.
An action such as Undo is optional.

orb.summary: The AI's mark. While work runs, a comet ring turns around the bot and the bot breathes. Done, it is a still wash.
usage: AI work looks alive: show the orb while it runs and the outputs as they arrive.
One AI mark per screen.

progress-ring.summary: A grey track and an accent arc for n of N stops of a tour.
usage: The arc animates between values.
Tour position lives in a sticky strip, not a counter in words.

breathing-dot.summary: The live marker: a 10dp accent dot that breathes.
usage: Use it for a thing that is happening now.

pending-dot.summary: A hollow 10dp ring for a step that has not started.
usage: Pair with OkDot and BreathingDot for the three states of a step.

ok-dot.summary: A 14dp green dot with a white tick, for a finished step.
usage: Pair with PendingDot and BreathingDot for the three states of a step.

skeleton.summary: A 12dp shimmering bar that stands in for text that is still being written. RowsSkeleton is a list's first rows built from it.
usage: Give it a width with the modifier.
Use it where the shape of the content is known, never as a loading screen.
RowsSkeleton stands in for the Inbox-style rows of a list that is still arriving, such as a repository's pull requests.

profile-dot.summary: The avatar placeholder: the warm gradient disc.
usage: Only where a real author photo is not available, and never as decoration.
